target_reference_entry: Chuyu Wang, Lei Xie, Yuancan Lin, Wei Wang, Yingying Chen, Yanling Bu, Kai Zhang, and Sanglu Lu. 2021. Thru-the-wall eavesdropping on loudspeakers via RFID by capturing sub-mm level vibration. In Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies, Vol. 5. 1–25.
paper_level_summary_zh: 该论文将目标论文列为RFID振动传感相关工作，但仅作为普通引文提及，未明确确认或使用其亚毫米级振动感知能力。

evidences.evidence_quote: Meanwhile, due to the excellent sensing ability of RF signals, recent years have witnessed the rapid development of RFID-based vibration sensing [29, 50, 55, 56, 58], which are generally utilized to sense mechanical vibrations.
evidences.evidence_context: However, due to the advantages of low cost and deployment flexibility, RFID tags have been widely utilized in various wireless sensing applications, such as localization [49], user authentication [8, 17], and vital signs monitoring [47], etc. Meanwhile, due to the excellent sensing ability of RF signals, recent years have witnessed the rapid development of RFID-based vibration sensing [29, 50, 55, 56, 58], which are generally utilized to sense mechanical vibrations. However, no existing works are available to realize online conversation eavesdropping through RFID sensing.
